sentences.text: This appeal by the claimant has been filed under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act arising out of award dated 23/11/2021 passed by Fifth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior in MACC No.9/2018 seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Fifth Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he has filed an application under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC (I.A.No.220/2024) for taking on record his pay slip, order regarding leave which could not be produced before the Claims Tribunal.
Therefore, learned Tribunal has erred in determining appellant's income and for just decision of the matter, these documents are necessary.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant also submits that if I.A with respect to above is allowed, then,
matter will have to be remitted back to Tribunal to decide the matter afresh.
5.

L e a r n e d counsel for the respondent-Insurance submits that if I.A.No.220/2024 filed by appellant is allowed, then, matter be remitted back so that they could also adduce evidence in rebuttal, if any.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. Para-29 of impugned award reveals that the Claims Tribunal has assessed the notional incomes of the appellant at Rs. 5,000/- per month; whereas, as per the documents produced alongiwth the application I.A.No. 220/2024, he was earning more than Rs. 22,000/- per month 8.

At appellate stage, learned counsel for the appellants filed I.A.No.220/2024 under Order 41 Rule 27 CPC and prayed to take on record these documents so that actual income of the appellant can be assessed and he can be awarded adequate award.

9. In view of above, in this Court's opinion, document filed by appellants along with I.A. are necessary and relevant for just decision of the case and appellant has stated reasons for not filing the same before the trial Court.
10. I n view of above, I.A.No. 220/2024 filed by appellant is allowed and documents filed along with the I.A are taken on record.

11. In view of above, present matter requires to be remitted back to Tribunal for affording opportunity to appellant to prove said documents as per law and to afford opportunity to respondents to adduce evidence in rebuttal, if any.

12. Hence, award passed by the Tribunal, is set aside and Tribunal is directed to afford an opportunity to appellant to adduce evidence in relation to documents produced alongwith application and thereafter, afford opportunity to respondents to adduce evidence in rebuttal, if any and after affording opportunity of hearing to both the side, decide the matter afresh on merits.

13 Parties are directed to remain present before Tribunal on 02.05.2024.
14.
Appeal filed by appellant is disposed of accordingly.
